target: The peduncle (PO:0009053) bears no bracts: bract (PO:0009055) absent (PATO:0000462), with 'peduncle' as context. The involucral bracts (PO:0009045) are present and puberulous (FLOPO:0991049).
fix: 'ebracteate' after 'peduncle', 'scape' or 'stem' means that axis has no bracts. Keep the axis as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'bract absent', which also denies the involucral bracts (phyllaries).
reason: Microseris heads always have phyllaries. FNA's 'ebracteate' is about the peduncle.

target: short shoot (PO:0004701, axillary leaf clusters, with 'axillary' as context) absent (PATO:0000462). The leaves are present. 'flexuous' (sinuous PATO:0001989) may belong to the leaves or to the stems.
fix: In Caryophyllaceae (FNA), 'axillary leaves absent/present' means axillary leaf fascicles, which are short shoots. Map it to short shoot (PO:0004701), never to leaf absent.
reason: Minuartia always has leaves. The FNA character is about axillary fascicles.

target: bract (PO:0009055) absent on the peduncle (PO:0009053 as context). 'sparsely tomentose' probably describes the phyllaries (involucral bract PO:0009045, tomentose PATO:0002341) or the peduncle itself, not peduncle bracts.
fix: Same rule as X02100: 'Peduncles ebracteate' denies bracts on the peduncle only. Keep 'peduncle' as context.
reason: Packera heads have phyllaries. The absence is limited to the peduncle.

target: phyllode leaf (PO:0025335) absent (PATO:0000462). The pitcher leaves (vascular leaf PO:0009025) are present. 'orifice oval' (elliptic PATO:0000947) describes the pitcher mouth, not the whole leaf.
fix: 'phyllodia', 'phyllodes' and 'phyllodium' are synonyms of phyllode leaf (PO:0025335). Their absence never falls back to leaf (PO:0025034). A pitcher 'orifice', 'mouth' or 'hood' quality needs that part as context.
reason: Sarracenia jonesii has pitchers but no flat phyllodes. The plant clearly has leaves.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO:0020138) with 'marginal' as context absent (PATO:0000462). The lamina is present. 'midrib flat' belongs on the leaf midvein (PO:0020139, flat PATO:0000407), not on the lamina.
fix: '<modifier> vein absent' (marginal, intramarginal, submarginal) denies that vein only. The bearer is leaf lamina vein (PO:0020138) with the modifier as context. 'midrib' maps to leaf midvein (PO:0020139), which is already its synonym.
reason: A leaf without a marginal vein still has a blade. Both statements dropped their vein noun.

target: The peduncle (PO:0009053) has no sterile bracts: bract (PO:0009055) absent, with 'peduncle' as context. The floral bracts (PO:0009055) are present and lanceolate (PATO:0001877).
fix: Same rule as X02100: 'Peduncle ebracteate' denies sterile bracts on the peduncle only. Floral bracts stay present.
reason: Orchids with an ebracteate peduncle still have floral bracts, and these are described.

target: petal (PO:0009032) with 'inner' as context absent (or minute). The outer petals are present and yellowish green.
fix: 'inner petals absent', 'outer petals absent' and 'inner whorl absent' deny one whorl only. Keep 'inner' or 'outer' as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'petal absent'.
reason: In Annona reticulata the inner petals are missing or vestigial, and the outer petals are the ones described.

target: One member is awnless (probably the lower floret's lemma (PO:0009037) or the glumes). The upper lemma carries the geniculate awn (PO:0025349, bent PATO:0000617).
fix: In grasses, 'awnless' sits in a clause about one member (lower glume, lower lemma, pedicelled spikelet). Keep that member as bearer or context. Never record a taxon-wide 'awn absent'.
reason: In Andropogoneae such as Apocopis, the upper lemma usually has a geniculate awn while other members have none.

target: Only the basal sheaths (leaf sheath PO:0020104, with 'basal' as context) have no blade. The leaf blades (PO:0020039) are present and linear (PATO:0001199).
fix: In Cyperaceae, 'bladeless sheaths' means those sheaths have no blade. Keep the sheath context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent' (same rule as X02090).
reason: Carex has bladeless basal sheaths with leaves above them that have blades.

target: The involucral bract is present but has no distinct leaflike blade. It is spathaceous (FLOPO:0991222): inflorescence bract (PO:0009054), spathaceous.
fix: 'without (distinct) bract leaf', 'bract not leaflike' and 'bract blade absent' mean the bract is reduced to a sheath or scale. Record the bract's shape, never bract absent.
reason: The same text describes the bract as spathelike, so the bract exists.

target: The inflorescence bracts (PO:0009054) are present and have no sheath (esheathing). Record the missing sheath, with 'bract' as context, or drop it. The glumes (PO:0009039) are present and lanceolate.
fix: '<part> without sheaths' or 'esheathing' denies a sheath on the part being described. It never means the part is absent.
reason: In Carex, the bracts are routinely described as sheathing or not, so the bracts themselves exist.

target: Only the basal leaves are absent: rosette leaf (PO:0000014), or leaf with 'basal' as context, absent. The cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are present and alternate (PATO:0001932).
fix: 'basal leaves absent' maps to rosette leaf (PO:0000014), or to leaf with 'basal' as context. Never drop 'basal' (same rule as X02097 for 'cauline').
reason: Cauline leaves are described in the same text.

target: The stem (scape) is leafless: cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. The basal leaves are present and tomentose (PATO:0002341).
fix: 'leafless' in a stem or scape clause means cauline leaves are absent. Never read it as leaf (PO:0025034) absent (same rule as X02085).
reason: Crepis bodinieri has a rosette of basal leaves on a leafless scape.

target: The female flowers (pistillate flower PO:0025599) have no petals. The male flowers (staminate flower PO:0025600) have oblong petals (PATO:0000946).
fix: In unisexual-flowered families (Euphorbiaceae and others), statements under 'Male flowers' or 'Female flowers' carry that sex. Keep it as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'petal absent'.
reason: Croton female flowers are typically apetalous or have reduced petals, while male flowers have petals.

target: Nothing is absent. The flowers were not seen on the material. Drop the absence. The inflorescence position (axillary or terminal) is probably taken from fruiting material and can stay.
fix: '<part> not seen', 'not known' or 'unknown' means the material was incomplete. Never read it as absent (PATO:0000462). Drop it (same rule as X02070).
reason: 'not seen' reports what the material showed. It says nothing about what the plant has.

target: On the culm sheath, leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent (PATO:0000462) and the oral setae absent. The culm sheath (leaf sheath PO:0020104, with 'culm' as context) is present and persistent (non-deciduous PATO:0001732).
fix: In bamboos, 'culm sheath' maps to leaf sheath (PO:0020104) with 'culm' as context, never to stipule. 'auricles' maps to leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106), and 'oral setae' to the setae on the sheath's shoulders, never to the sheath or stipule.
reason: Bamboos have no stipules. Both statements were sent to stipule, which made a false contradiction.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent on the culm sheath. The culm sheath (leaf sheath PO:0020104, with 'culm' as context) is present and has prominent longitudinal ribs (ribbed FLOPO:0991062).
fix: Same rule as X02115: in bamboos, 'culm sheath' never maps to stipule, and 'auricles absent' maps to leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106).
reason: The ribs show the sheath exists. Only its auricles are missing.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent. The leaves are present, and their blade margins are rolled (curled PATO:0000405 on leaf margin PO:0020128).
fix: 'auricles absent' in grasses and bamboos maps to leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106). Never fall back to leaf (PO:0025034) or its parent.
reason: Missing auricles are a feature of the sheath. They do not mean the plant has no leaves.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent (PATO:0000462) and oral setae absent. Remove the 'present' record made from the same phrase.
fix: In 'X and Y absent', 'absent' applies to every coordinated noun. Never record the first noun as present because only the last one sits next to 'absent'. One phrase must not give both present and absent for one part.
reason: Both records come from the same text. The negation was lost for 'auricles'.

target: involucral bract (PO:0009045), or inflorescence bract (PO:0009054) with 'involucral' as context, absent. Do not record bract (PO:0009055) absent. The glumes (PO:0009039) are present and NOT mucronate: the quality record also lost its negation.
fix: 'involucral bracts absent' must map to the specific bract term. Never use the general bract (PO:0009055), whose absence also denies glumes and bracteoles, which are kinds of bract in PO. Also, 'not <quality>' must never be recorded as '<quality>'.
reason: Fimbristylis spikelets always have glumes. The absence was widened to all bracts.

target: flower (PO:0009046) with 'sterile' (the showy marginal flowers) as context absent. The fertile flowers and the corymbose inflorescence are present.
fix: 'sterile flowers absent', 'ray flowers absent' and 'marginal flowers absent' deny one kind of flower. Keep the modifier as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'flower absent' (same rule as X02086).
reason: In Hydrangea the enlarged sterile marginal flowers are optional. The fertile flowers are always there.

target: Nothing is absent. The flowers are unknown to the authors, so drop the absence. The axillary position probably comes from the infructescence and can stay.
fix: Same rule as X02114: 'not known' means the material was incomplete. Drop it.
reason: 'Flowers not known' is a gap in the material, not an absence in the plant.

target: Nothing is absent. Only the male flowers (staminate flower PO:0025600) are unknown, so drop the absence. The female flowers or fruits carry the axillary inflorescence.
fix: Same rule as X02114. Also, an unknown part with a sex modifier must never become a taxon-wide 'flower absent'.
reason: Ilex is dioecious, and the authors saw only female or fruiting material.

target: The stem is almost leafless (few or no cauline leaves, PO:0000013). Drop the absence or record it as reduced. The basal leaves are present, with an attenuate base (PATO:0001982).
fix: 'almost', 'nearly', 'subleafless' or 'apparently' leafless describes how an axis looks. Never read it as an absence (same rule as X02072).
reason: 'almost' hedges the statement, and the basal leaves are described.

target: The frond (FLOPO_0985026) is present and has no green stalk at its base. Record the missing stalk (PO:0025066, with 'frond' as context) or drop it. The frond, not a leaf, is shiny bright green (PATO:0000320).
fix: 'without <structure> at base' denies the structure, not the part being described. In Lemnaceae, 'frond' maps to frond (FLOPO_0985026), never to leaf (PO:0025034).
reason: Lemna fronds lack the stalk that some relatives have. The fronds clearly exist.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO:0020138) with 'marginal' as context absent. The lateral veins (PO:0020138 with 'lateral' as context) are present and numerous.
fix: Same rule as X02104: '<modifier> vein absent' keeps the modifier. Never record vascular bundle (PO:0005020) absent for the whole plant.
reason: A vascular plant cannot lack vascular bundles. Only the marginal vein is missing.

target: The involucre at the base of the umbel has no bracts (bract PO:0009055, 'involucre' as context). The bracteoles of the involucel (bract PO:0009055 via its synonym 'bracteole', 'involucel' as context) are present and linear (PATO:0001199).
fix: In Apiaceae, 'bracts' means the involucre and 'bracteoles' means the involucel. Keep them apart as context. PO lists 'bracteole' as a synonym of bract, so without context the two merge and contradict.
reason: Oenanthe often has no involucre bracts but has linear involucel bracteoles.

target: One kind of sheath lacks auricles while the other has them (leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106). In bamboo descriptions this is usually culm sheath versus foliage-leaf sheath. Keep 'culm sheath' or 'foliage leaf sheath' as context.
fix: In bamboos, the culm sheaths and the foliage-leaf sheaths are described separately. An auricle statement takes the sheath of its paragraph or clause as context, never a taxon-wide auricle.
reason: Oligostachyum descriptions treat culm sheaths and leaf sheaths in separate sections, and their auricles often differ.

target: Nothing is absent. The stipules (PO:0020041) are present and caducous (deciduous (generic) PATO:0001730). They had fallen off the specimens. Drop the absence.
fix: 'caducous, not seen' and 'early deciduous, not seen' mean the part fell off before collection. Record the caducous quality only. 'not seen' is never an absence.
reason: The same phrase gives the reason the stipules were not seen.

target: Nothing is absent. Drop the 'not seen' record. The stipules (PO:0020041) are caducous (PATO:0001730). The 'not seen' may also belong to another part in its own clause.
fix: A bare 'not seen' (or 'not seen' attached by distance) is never an absence. Drop it (same rule as X02114).
reason: Caducous stipules exist. They had fallen off the specimens.
